title: Atomic emission metering with KV-offset model
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: produce a production-ready, per-emitted-token metering surface that attributes latency and unit cost at the finest practical granularity while accounting for KV/prefix cache effects using an offset model. The 'KV-offset' idea: when a cache hit prevents some portion of kernel work, emit a negative offset token-cost event tied to the request so downstream billing/reconciliation subtracts the saved work instead of overstating emission cost.

Background: current cost reports are token-count and coarse latency buckets. This causes mismatches between runtime economics (GPU kernel work, KV fetches) and billing. We need microsecond-level probes in the serving runtime plus an enrichment pipeline that converts spans into per-lexeme charge events.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change customer billing contracts. It builds the instrumentation and reconciliation pipeline and publishes dashboards/alerts for internal ops and accounting teams. Final billing export will be reviewed with finance in a follow-up.

Technical approach:
1) Runtime tracing hooks: add lightweight per-emit probes that record microsecond deltas for: prefix cache lookup, kv-fetch, kv-deserialize, kernel-exec (decode+attn+proj), token-serialize. Spans/tags to emit: span names: request.recv, cache.lookup, kv.fetch, kernel.exec, emit.token_{index}. Tags: request_id, model, model_variant, seq_len, token_index, cache_hit (true/false), kv_latency_ms, kernel_latency_us, emission_bytes. Probe must be toggleable and sampled.
2) Atomic emission events: bundle per-token microtimings into a compact protobuf/JSON event: {request_id, model, token_index, kernel_us, kv_us, cache_hit, timestamp, sequence_pos}. We will send to the metrics/log pipeline as structured logs to the ingestion topic.
3) KV-offset model: when cache_hit=true we will produce an additional event with negative 'work_units' equal to the estimated saved kernel_us for that token. This enables ledger-style reconciliation that adds positive work for executed tokens and subtracts saved work for cache hits so aggregates align with actual GPU cycles consumed.
4) Metrics pipeline: structured logs -> Kafka -> Flink enrichment -> ClickHouse/BigQuery. We will add a lightweight Flink job that translates events into two derived tables: token_emissions (granular) and token_offsets (cache savings).
5) Dashboards & alerts: Console panels for: p50/p95 per-token kernel_us, KV hit rate by model/route, aggregate offset ratio (offset_us / executed_us), top 10 routes by unaccounted time, anomalies where offsets exceed 60% of executed_us (indicative of double-counting).
6) Sampling & performance: default sampling=10% for production, 100% for requests > 5s or error status. Probe path must add <1% p99 latency overhead in microbench.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits token-level events in the new compact schema for sampled requests.
- Flink job ingests events and populates token_emissions and token_offsets within 2 minutes of emission.
- Console dashboard panels show correct aggregates and an example route demonstrates offsets reducing apparent cost when cache hits occur.
- Unit and integration tests for probe serialization and Flink enrichment are merged.
- Performance regression: end-to-end p99 latency increase from instrumentation <= 1%.

Rollout plan: dev -> staging (10% sampling) -> canary in prod (single region, routes with low traffic) -> full prod sampling. Monitoring during canary: cpu/gpu utilization, probe error rate, ingestion lag, and offset ratio.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sampled requests for runtime-1.20 produce compact token events with fields: request_id, model, variant, token_index, kernel_us, kv_us, cache_hit, timestamp. 2) Flink enrichment job writes token_emissions and token_offsets tables with <2m lag. 3) Console dashboards display offset-adjusted cost graphs for at least 3 routes and a synthetic test demonstrating a 30%-80% cost delta when cache enabled vs disabled. 4) No measurable >1% p99 latency regression across standard load test harness. 5) Tests and PRs merged and tagged for runtime-1.20 release.
updates: 2026-03-03 - Spike complete: microbench shows per-token probe serialization adds ~120ns avg, ~0.8% to p99 under synthetic gpt-like workload. Excerpted results in /drive/spikes/token-probe-microbench.md.

2026-03-05 - Design review: alignment with billing team. Finance confirmed offset approach is acceptable for internal recon; external billing change will be separate. Action: include offset metadata to ensure traceability to request and commit ID.

2026-03-08 - PR opened for runtime hooks (draft): github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/2386. Initial feedback: make probe message binary-protobuf to reduce ingestion cost; validating and adding schema.proto.

2026-03-10 - Flink enrichment prototype completed. Writes small test table in staging ClickHouse. Found edge-case where token_index restarts on partial retries; decided to include attempt_id in event. Patch in staging job submitted: github.com/redwood/observability/pulls/112.
2026-03-12 - Canary gating added: a feature flag in config server so we can toggle KV-offset emission per-customer. Added config key: tracing.emit_token_events. Ops to coordinate before prod canary.

2026-03-14 - Integration test failing intermittently: offsets exceeding executed_us for long prefix reuse cases. Action: add sanity clamp in Flink to floor offset at 80% of executed_us per-request and follow up with root-cause analysis (possible double-counting on prefix replay).
notes_for_engineering_review: Key trade-offs: 1) probe sampling vs accuracy: 10% reduces ingestion cost but requires robust extrapolation for billing analytics; 2) binary protobuf reduces bandwidth but increases serialization cost—bench shows net win; 3) offset clamping to avoid negative-net-work must be product-reviewed. Need review from runtime, infra (Flink), and billing owners before merging.
